newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army pushes further into Tiger territory.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army pushes further into Tiger territory.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops were digging in on Friday after advancing deeper into Tamil Tiger rebel-held territory, the Defence Ministry said on the fourth day of the armed forces' biggest push this year.
But it remained tight-lipped about their target.

The ministry's operational headquarters said in a statement that the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Ealam (LTTE), who are fighting for a minority Tamil homeland in the north and east, had offered no resistance.
"Troops on EDIBALA (brave force) Operation have advanced 22 km (14 miles) into enemy territory," the ministry statement said.

Backed by artillery, air force bombers and tanks, the army launched the advance from Vavuniya, a key government outpost 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, on Tuesday, Sri Lanka's Independence Day.

A ministry spokesman declined to reveal the location of the army units or where they were headed, but military officials in the area told Reuters troops were advancing in two thrusts, heading north and west from Vavuniya.
The officials, who declined to be named, said one flank had reached a key road junction about 20 km (12 miles) west of Vavuniya.
The road leads to Madhu village dominated by rebel bases and training camps. Madhu houses a historic Christian shrine.
It was not immediately clear if the advancing troops would head towards Madhu or turn north towards the government-held town of Kilinochchi, 70 km (50 miles) to Vavuniya's north.
In a statement on their Internet web site, the LTTE accused the government of attacking civilians during the troops' advance.
"Early reports suggest there is already a significant civilian death toll with local families taken by surprise and the young and old completely disoriented," the statement said.

"The unrestrained character of this latest military offensive confirms many observers' fears that an intensive effort to diminish the north-east Tamil population was being prepared by Sri Lanka," the LTTE statement said.
It did not give details of civilian casualties.
"That statement is wrong. The military does not attack villages nor does it kill civilians. We safeguard both," the ministry spokesman said.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the 14-year old conflict but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
